cards.text: This psalm opens with praise: "Hallelujah! Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever." Then the writer tells Israel's history, and friend, it's an HONEST one.

cards.question: The writer asks who can describe the mighty acts of the LORD or fully proclaim His praise. What's he getting at?

cards.text: Then he says who's blessed: those who uphold justice and practice righteousness at all times. At ALL times, friend, not just when somebody's watching the cookie box.
Now he gets personal. He asks the LORD to remember him and to visit him with His salvation.

cards.question: True or false: the writer wants the LORD's salvation so he can rejoice along with God's people.

cards.text: Then he confesses: "We have sinned like our fathers; we have done wrong and acted wickedly." No excuses at all, and friend, I once blamed a lopsided cookie on the oven for a WEEK when the problem was ME.

cards.question: The writer starts with Israel's fathers back in Egypt, who saw God's wonders up close. True or false: they remembered His abundant kindness.
Fresh out of Egypt, where does the psalm say Israel's fathers rebel?

cards.text: So they rebel right there by the sea, and you'd think that's the end of the road for them. But He saves them anyway.

cards.question: God saved them anyway, for the sake of His name and to make His ___ known.

cards.text: He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up, and He led them through the depths as through a desert. A whole SEA dried up, friend, and I can't even keep my counter dry when somebody rinses a mixing bowl.

cards.question: God saves Israel from the enemy that hated them, and the waters come back over that enemy. True or false: a few of the enemy make it out.
Their enemies are gone. How do the people respond right then?

answers.text: They believe and sing His praise
They ask to go back to Egypt
They build an altar of stones

cards.text: But it's not a happy ending yet: "Yet they soon forgot His works and failed to wait for His counsel." I walk into the pantry and forget the sprinkles, but these folks walked out of a SEA and forgot THAT.

cards.question: Out in the wilderness, they craved intensely and ___ God in the desert.
God gives the people what they asked for in the wilderness. What does He send along with it?

cards.text: Back in the camp, jealousy moves in. I know that look, friend, because it's the face I make at a baker's perfect batch when mine came out flat.

cards.question: In the camp in the wilderness, who do the people envy?

cards.text: That's Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron, the holy one of the LORD. Two men in this mess are Dathan and Abiram, who rose up against Moses (Numbers 16:1-2).

cards.question: True or false: when the earth opens up under the rebels, Dathan gets away.

cards.text: The earth swallowed Dathan and covered Abiram's group. Then fire blazed through their company, and flames consumed the wicked.

cards.question: Next, at Horeb, the people make a molten image and worship it. What is it?

cards.text: The psalm says they exchanged their Glory for the image of a grass-eating ox. A statue. Of an ox. That eats GRASS.

cards.question: At Horeb, they ___ God their Savior, who did great things in Egypt.

cards.text: That's the God of awesome deeds by the Red Sea, the One they just traded for a statue. So He said He would destroy them.

cards.question: Someone stood before God in the breach to turn His wrath away from destroying the people. Who?
Next, the psalm turns to the pleasant land and to God's promise. True or false: the people believed His promise.

cards.text: They despised the pleasant land, grumbled in their tents and didn't listen to the voice of the LORD. Grumbling in the tent is the group chat the boss isn't in.

cards.question: So the LORD raises His hand and swears an oath about the grumbling people. What does He swear?

answers.text: To cast them down in the wilderness
To lead them straight into the land
To give them a king like the nations

cards.text: He also swore to scatter their offspring among the nations. Keep that one in your apron pocket, friend.
Then they yoked themselves to Baal of Peor, a false god.

cards.question: At Baal of Peor, the people eat sacrifices. What does the psalm say those sacrifices were offered to?

cards.text: Their deeds provoked the LORD to anger, and a plague broke out among them. Then one man stands up: Phinehas, Aaron's grandson (Numbers 25:11).

cards.question: True or false: when Phinehas stood and intervened, the plague was restrained.
What Phinehas did was credited to him as ___ for endless generations to come.

cards.text: Next, the waters of Meribah. They angered the LORD there, and trouble came to Moses because of them.

cards.question: At the waters of Meribah, the people rebelled against His Spirit. What does Moses do?

cards.text: Once they're in the land, they don't destroy the peoples there, even though the LORD had commanded it.

cards.question: Instead of destroying the peoples in the land, what does Israel do with those nations?
Israel worshiped the idols of those nations, and the idols became a ___ to them.

cards.text: This is the heaviest part of the psalm. They sacrificed their sons and daughters to the idols of Canaan, and the land was polluted with blood.
The psalm says they defiled themselves by their actions and prostituted themselves by their deeds.

cards.question: True or false: after all Israel has done, the LORD lets it go without anger.
He delivered them into the hand of the nations, and those who ___ them ruled over them.

cards.text: Their enemies oppressed them and subdued them under their hand. At the sea, the waters covered their foes, but now the foes are on top.

Many times He rescued them, but they were bent on rebellion and sank down in their iniquity. You know when somebody gets rescued from a stuck elevator and then pushes the button for that SAME elevator?

cards.question: Israel keeps rebelling and sinks down in iniquity, and then they're in distress. What does God do?

answers.text: He sends them a new law

cards.question: God hears Israel's cry and relents. What does the psalm say He remembers?

cards.text: He relented by the abundance of His loving devotion. That's the same loving devotion from the start of this psalm, still there and still enduring.

cards.question: True or false: God made Israel objects of compassion to all who held them captive.

cards.text: Then the writer turns all of this history into a prayer.

cards.question: The writer asks the LORD to save His people and gather them from the nations. Why does he ask for this?

answers.text: So they can give thanks to His name
So they can defeat their enemies
So they can take back their land

cards.text: He closes by blessing the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting, tells all the people to say amen, and ends right where he started: "Hallelujah!" Go ahead, baker, say it, because mine comes out a little muffled through the mustache but it COUNTS.
